question: Should experimental Claws own and later remove globally named MCP server configuration before the Claws RFC compatibility contract is accepted?
rationale: The branch establishes a new owner for executable global configuration, while the open RFC treats the implementation stack as prototype evidence and reserves compatibility acceptance for a later decision.

options.title: Keep as gated prototype
options.body: Fix consent and proof now, but keep this PR draft and experimental until the RFC owner approves the ownership and upgrade contract.

options.title: Defer MCP mutation
options.body: Keep MCP declarations inspectable and exportable, but remove add/remove configuration mutation until the RFC is accepted.

recommendation.title: Keep as gated prototype
recommendation.body: Fix consent and proof now, but keep this PR draft and experimental until the RFC owner approves the ownership and upgrade contract.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current-main ownership history for MCP operator configuration and shared-state behavior.
